introH2: 🏖️ How many kinds of Bangsaen beachfront stays are there, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Bangsaen is the beach that people from Bangkok drive to for an easy day trip, but when it comes to actually finding somewhere to stay overnight right by the sea, a lot of people are surprised there aren't as many options as they'd think — and the ones that exist look very different from each other. Some are beachfront resorts where you cross one road to reach the sea, with a nice pool that suits families. Some are serviced apartments with sea-view rooms and kitchens that work for longer stays. And some are small design boutiques that sell atmosphere more than room count. Another thing many people are still unclear on is that Bangsaen has two beach zones — main Bangsaen Beach, which is lively and packed with shops, and Wonnapha Beach to the south, which is quieter and more private. This article rounds up 9 Bangsaen beachfront stays we've reviewed in depth across both beach zones. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews — we give both the upsides and the honest caveats, we didn't stay ourselves, we compare prices across 3 sites, and we include all the direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Bangsaen has no train line, and public transport in the area is still thin, so having your own car is the easiest way to get around. From Bangkok it's about an hour and a half on the motorway or Bang Na–Trat highway, and around 1 hour 15 minutes from Suvarnabhumi Airport. Without a car you can take a van or bus to Chonburi town, then continue by songthaew or ride-hail into Bangsaen. The stays in this article sit in two zones: main Bangsaen Beach (around the roundabout) — lively, with plenty of restaurants and beachside food, easy to walk down to the water and head out to eat; and Wonnapha Beach (to the south, near the fish pier and Burapha University) — quieter and more private, good for a calm break. The two zones are close together, just a few minutes' walk or drive apart, and near Nong Mon Market, Khao Sam Muk, and the Institute of Marine Science.

entries.name: The Tide Resort Bangsaen
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.2 · 294 reviews · TripAdvisor #1 in Saen Suk subdistrict
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On Bangsaen Beach · cross the road to the sea
tags: 🏖️ Cross the road to the sea
entries.addr: 44/1 Bang Saen Sai 1 Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If we had to pick just one Bangsaen beachfront stay to send a friend, we'd start with The Tide Resort Bangsaen, because it's one of the first names people in Chonburi and Bangkok think of — and the score backs that up: 9.2 from 294 reviews on Trip.com, and TripAdvisor ranks it #1 of 10 hotels in Saen Suk subdistrict. It's a 4-star beachfront resort on Bang Saen Sai 1 Road set in a shady garden, and the selling point is clear: cross the road in front of the resort and you're on the sand and in the sea — just over an hour's drive from Bangkok and you're falling asleep to the sound of waves. What reviews agree on is the two pools split into adult and kids' zones, with a slide the children love, clean water, and several good photo spots, especially in the late afternoon. Another thing people praise is the curved balconies on the higher-tier rooms that look out over the sea and garden — a favorite morning coffee spot — plus enough on-site parking, which is very hard to find in Bangsaen on weekends. One important thing to know is that the resort has now rebranded as Amari Bangsaen under the ONYX group; the building and pools are the same, so when booking look for "Amari Bangsaen (Formerly The Tide Resort)" to avoid confusion. The honest caveats from reviews: some rooms look older than the website photos and are mid-way through being brought up to the new brand's standard, breakfast still isn't as impressive as many expect from a 4-star resort, and on weekends the beach road gets busy and congested. Best for families bringing kids to swim, and couples who want the sea close to Bangkok and an overnight by the beach in a calm setting.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Search for "Amari Bangsaen (Formerly The Tide Resort)" on booking platforms · ask for a higher-tier room with a curved sea-view balcony and check whether it's one of the renovated rooms · on holidays arrive early and rely mainly on the resort's parking.

Beachfront, cross the road to the sea, just over an hour from Bangkok
Two pools with a slide, clean water, good for families
Curved sea-view balconies in higher-tier rooms · enough on-site parking
cons: Some rooms look older than the photos and are mid-transition to the Amari brand
Breakfast still isn't as impressive as you'd expect from a 4-star resort (per reviews)

entries.type: Seaside Service Apartment, 3-star · sea-view rooms + kitchen
entries.name: BBG Seaside Luxurious Service Apartment
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.0 · TripAdvisor 4.5/5 · #2 specialty lodging in Bangsaen
entries.badge: 🌊 Every room a sea view + kitchen
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wonnapha Beach · near Burapha Univ. · by the sea
tags: 🌊 Every room a sea view + balcony
entries.addr: 108/81 Bang Saen Sai 1 Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If you want a "temporary home by the sea" more than a small hotel room, BBG Seaside Luxurious Service Apartment is the name we want you to know. It's a serviced apartment on Wonnapha Beach, the quieter side compared with main Bangsaen Beach, in a roughly 6-storey building with only about 24–25 rooms, so it never feels crowded. The thing it takes all the way is that every room is a sea-view room with a balcony and an in-room kitchen — fridge, stove, microwave — in sizes from about 40 to 80 sqm in one- and two-bedroom layouts. Many real reviews call it the best location in Bangsaen they've stayed at: rooms are spacious and clean, beds are comfortable, you wake up and open the curtains to the sea, and there's a Thai breakfast served to the room. Staff also get praise for being friendly and checking guests in fast. The score is 9.0 from 71 reviews on Trip.com and 4.5/5 on TripAdvisor (#2 of 11 specialty lodging stays in Bangsaen). The honest caveats: there's no pool, and the sea in front sits beside the fish pier, so you can't swim there — it's better for looking at; to swim you'll need to go to main Bangsaen Beach. The building opened back in 2014, so some fittings are starting to age, and the location is toward the end of the road, so without a car it's harder to get around than stays in the middle of the beach. Best for couples, families, long-stay guests, and parents visiting their kids at Burapha University who want space, an in-room kitchen, and a sea view in every room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specifically ask for a room not blocked by the fish pier for a full Gulf of Thailand view · for a group or a long stay choose a two-bedroom room with a kitchen and ask about weekly/monthly rates · driving yourself is easiest given the end-of-road location and free parking.
pros: Every room is a sea-view room with a balcony, a full Gulf of Thailand view
A real, usable in-room kitchen in every unit, good for long stays and self-catering
Spacious 40–80 sqm rooms, quiet and private · walking distance to Burapha Univ.
Friendly staff, fast check-in · Thai breakfast served to the room
cons: No pool · the sea in front sits beside the fish pier, so you can't swim there
End-of-road location, harder to get around without a car
Building opened in 2014, some fittings are starting to age (per reviews)

entries.type: Resort, 3-star · studio rooms with kitchen by the pool
entries.name: Le Casa Bang Saen Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.8 · 68 reviews · TripAdvisor #1 guesthouse in Bangsaen
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Bangsaen · near Burapha Univ. (deep down a soi)
entries.addr: 13/14 Long Hat Bang Saen Soi 1, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: Bangsaen in many people's memory is a lively, traffic-jammed, noisy beach — but Le Casa Bang Saen Hotel gives the surprisingly opposite feeling. It's a 3-star in-town resort tucked down Long Hat Bang Saen Soi 1 near Burapha University, with several buildings arranged around a central pool and garden, so almost every room gets a balcony looking onto the pool or the green garden, making it shadier and quieter than most people expect for this area. What guests talk about most is the studio rooms that are larger than the 3-star average, decorated in warm oak furniture, with a small in-room kitchen, which makes it great for multi-night stays where you want to reheat food or make your own coffee. The star of the common area is the outdoor pool with a built-in jacuzzi, ringed by garden and room blocks; reviews say it's clean, the water is clear, and it's quiet. What people who drive really like is the large free parking lot for about 40–50 cars with an attendant — many can park right outside their room, which is very rare in Bangsaen. The score is 8.8 from 68 reviews on Trip.com, and #1 among Bangsaen guesthouses on TripAdvisor. The honest caveats from reviews: the resort sits deep down a soi, so it's about a 5-minute walk out to the main road, it's not beachfront where you can walk straight into the water (about 1.7 km from the beach, a 10-minute walk), some rooms' furniture is starting to age, and breakfast has limited choices and is sometimes not served hot. Best for families, couples, and groups of friends who drive and want a spacious room with a kitchen, a quiet setting, and convenient parking on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specifically ask for a room with a balcony overlooking the pool, the view guests rate highest · make the most of the in-room kitchen on a long stay by buying ingredients from Nong Mon Market to cook · without a car, have a ride-hail app ready since the resort is deep down a soi.

entries.type: Budget Resort, 3-star · sea-view rooms by the beach
entries.name: Coco Beach Resort Bangsaen
entries.badge: 🥥 Sea view in the low thousands · best value
tags: 🥥 Sea-view rooms in the low thousands
entries.addr: 20/9 Bang Saen Lang Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If you want to wake up, open the curtains, and see the Bangsaen sea without paying luxury-resort prices, Coco Beach Resort Bangsaen sells one thing and sells it decisively: sea-view rooms by Bangsaen Beach in the low thousands. It's a 3-star, 45-room resort on Bang Saen Lang Road, about a 5-minute walk from the beach, in an area full of restaurants and roadside food. Its location score on Trip.com hits 9.2, the highest of all its rating categories, with cleanliness at 9.1. The real standout is the Deluxe Sea View rooms with a balcony where you get a full view of the Bangsaen sea — the main reason people choose it and come back. Reviews agree the rooms are clean, more spacious than expected for the price, beds are comfortable, the air-con is cold, staff are friendly, and there's free parking that solves the very tight beachfront parking situation on weekends. It earns an overall 8.8 from 64 reviews, which is high for this price tier. The honest caveats from reviews: the walls are fairly thin, so you can hear the next room, especially on busy weekends; some rooms' in-room Wi-Fi signal isn't strong; the bathroom and pool are fairly small; and breakfast isn't included in the rate and has to be ordered separately by the dish. Sea-view rooms are limited to about 10 of the 45, so they sell out fast in high season. Best for couples and families who want a sea-view room by the beach, walking distance to the sand, with a pool and parking, on a low-thousands budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's worth paying extra to choose a Deluxe Sea View room from the start, since they're limited and are the biggest draw · if you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room not sharing a wall, or a floor with fewer people, and bring earplugs · check the breakfast situation before booking, as it's mostly ordered separately, not a buffet.
pros: Deluxe sea-view rooms with a balcony, in the low thousands, great value

entries.type: Hotel & Residence, 4-star · spacious rooms with kitchen
entries.name: ONPA Hotel & Residence Bangsaen
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.5 · 368 reviews (most in the newer-stay group)
entries.badge: 🏠 Spacious rooms with kitchen · lots of reviews
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wonnapha Beach · ~300 m from the beach
tags: 🏠 Spacious rooms in several layouts with kitchen
entries.addr: 112 Na De Di Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If Bangsaen in your memory is a small hotel room you can only stay in for a night or two, ONPA Hotel & Residence Bangsaen paints a different picture. It's a 4-star, 160-unit serviced apartment and hotel on Na De Di Road, on the Wonnapha Beach side that's quieter than main Bangsaen Beach. Among Bangsaen's newer stays, it has the most reviews in this article — 368 on Trip.com, with a score of 8.5. What sets ONPA apart from typical Bangsaen stays is its residence-style rooms — spacious rooms in several layouts, from studios to two-bedroom 60 sqm suites, many with a kitchenette plus microwave, a seating corner, and a dining corner, designed to live in for several days like a small home. Real reviews agree the rooms are spacious for the price, clean, with comfortable beds, and what drivers really like is the roomy parking with no scramble for a spot, which is hard to find in Bangsaen on weekends. There's an outdoor pool, a gym, a ping-pong table, a playground, and a 24-hour front desk. It's only about 300 meters from Wonnapha Beach, a few minutes' walk. The honest caveats from reviews: Western breakfast options are still limited for international visitors, some rooms have a slightly stale smell from being closed up, the pool water's clarity isn't consistent at times, and it's not a beachfront resort — you walk to the beach yourself. Best for families, groups of friends, and long-stay guests in Bangsaen who want a spacious room with a kitchen on an affordable budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a group, choose a one- or two-bedroom residence room with a kitchen and seating corner — better value than booking several studios · check that the room you pick has a kitchen and microwave before booking, as not all do · ask to run the air-con for ventilation against any stale smell from check-in.

entries.type: Boutique, 3-star · design boutique with a curved building
entries.name: Kalm Bangsaen Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.3 · 16 reviews · TripAdvisor #2 stay in Bangsaen
entries.badge: 🎨 Curved design · sea views for nearly half the building
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bangsaen · 5–10 min walk to the beach
entries.addr: 6 Soi 10, Bang Saen Lang Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If thinking of Bangsaen brings to mind only plain, boxy hotel buildings, Kalm Bangsaen Hotel changes that the moment you see it. It's a 3-star boutique hotel with just 21 rooms, designed by junnarchitect with a curved building instead of an ordinary rectangle, genuinely playing on the word "calm" in the name Kalm. The cleverness of the curved design isn't just for looks — it angles the rooms so that nearly half of all 21 rooms can face the sea, while the rest look onto the long pool that runs parallel to the building. The star here is the sea-view rooms that come with a private balcony and a bathtub — sip coffee on the balcony looking at the sea in the morning, or soak in the tub to relax after a walk on the beach, which guests agree is worth the price difference. The common area has a saltwater pool that's gentle on skin and eyes, the atmosphere is quiet and lives up to the name, and staff get praise for the warm service of a small boutique. The score is 8.3 from 16 reviews on Trip.com and #2 stay in Bangsaen on TripAdvisor. The honest caveats from reviews: the sea-view rooms face Bang Saen Lang Road, which has passing traffic, so light sleepers will hear cars, especially on busy weekends; some standard rooms are starting to look older than the sea-view rooms; some bathrooms are compact; and parking is limited to the hotel's size. Best for couples or small groups who want a good-looking design stay with a sea-view room, balcony, and bathtub, coming to chill and take photos more than to power through activities all day.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If the budget allows, just pay extra for a sea-view room with a balcony and bathtub · if you're sensitive to noise, ask for a high floor and bring earplugs, or choose a quieter pool-view room · with only 21 rooms and sea-view rooms selling out fast, book ahead for weekends.

entries.name: Bangsaen Heritage Hotel
entries.revCount: Across multiple platforms, around 8.1 · over 4,000 reviews (most in the set)
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Across from Bangsaen Beach · Mueang Chonburi
tags: 🏡 Choose a room or a villa
entries.addr: 50, 54 Bang Saen Sai 1 Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: Among Bangsaen's beachfront stays, if you measure by "how much people talk about it," Bangsaen Heritage Hotel has the biggest review base in this set by a wide margin — over 4,000 reviews across multiple platforms, with a score around 8.1. It's a 4-star midrange hotel set directly across from the beach, so you cross the road to reach the sand, and it's big enough — nearly 300 rooms and villas combined — to take families and group trips. What makes it different from a typical hotel is that it's not just rooms in a building: there's also a garden villa zone in a contemporary Thai-house style to choose from, from one-bedroom villas up to a Two-Bedroom Pool Villa with its own private pool, good for groups who want to swim privately. The star here for families is the pool with a slide that kids can play on all day, a separate kids' pool, and a lifeguard on duty, plus free parking and a breakfast that many reviews call better than expected for this tier. Staff also get praise for friendliness, and there are returning regulars who come back many times. The honest caveat that has to be stated clearly: room condition is inconsistent — the hotel only began gradually renovating some rooms and villas in 2024 (names starting with Premier); rooms not yet renovated show wear, peeling paint, and old furniture, some reviews complain the beds are firm, the pool is fairly small for the room count, and the innermost villas are a long walk from the common area. Best for families and groups of friends who want an easy Bangsaen overnight with a pool for kids and villas to stay in together, on a budget of no more than the low two-thousands per night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specifically request a Premier-group room or villa renovated in 2024 when booking and confirm at check-in for a clearly better condition · for a group, splitting a 2-bedroom villa beats booking several rooms · if you're with elderly guests, ask for a villa near the common area.
pros: Biggest review base in the set, over 4,000 reviews · across from the beach, walk straight to the sea
Choose either an in-building room or a garden villa, some with a private pool

cons: Room condition is inconsistent — not-yet-renovated rooms are old, with peeling paint and old furniture

entries.type: Beachfront, 3-star · colorful design on Wonnapha Beach
entries.name: Coasta Bangsaen
entries.badge: 🎨 Colorful by the beach · cross the road to the sea
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wonnapha Beach · cross the road to the sea
tags: 🏖️ Cross the road to Wonnapha Beach
entries.addr: 15/3 Soi 4, Bang Saen Lang Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: If you've ever driven along Wonnapha Beach and your eye caught a bright, European-style building, that's Coasta Bangsaen. It's a 3-star beachfront hotel on the Wonnapha-side beach road, a spot known to be quieter and more private than main Bangsaen Beach. The clear selling point is that you cross the road in front of the hotel to reach the beach, and the Studio sea-view rooms have a balcony where you get a full view of the sunset. The building is painted in bright colors that make it a landmark and photograph nicely. What real reviews most agree on is that the rooms are spacious for the price, with a big, comfortable bed, and a bigger bathroom than expected, plus a pool to cool off after the beach, an elevator, a 24-hour counter, and free parking. Prices start at just around ฿1,300/night, which is a very light budget for a stay that's a road-crossing from the beach. But to be honest, reviews are fairly split into two camps: those who love it for the location, and those let down by the upkeep. The honest caveats: the building opened back in 2012 (renovated 2015), so some rooms have age-related details to keep an eye on, like slow-draining bathroom water or some older fittings, cleanliness in some rooms isn't consistent, and breakfast depends on the package — some packages don't include it. The Wonnapha side still relies mainly on having your own car. Best for couples and groups of friends who want a Wonnapha beachfront stay on a budget, a road-crossing from the sea, with spacious rooms and a balcony for the sunset, setting expectations to match a 3-star price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose and specifically request a Studio sea-view room when booking, as they're limited and sell out fast · read the package details clearly on whether breakfast is included · the building opened in 2012, so if you find something that needs fixing, tell the counter right away to ask for a room change.

Rooms are spacious for the price, big bed, bigger bathroom than expected

entries.name: Panitar Haus
entries.badge: 🌅 Rooftop infinity pool for the sunset
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wonnapha Beach · walk to the beach · near the roundabout
tags: 🌅 Rooftop infinity pool with a sea view
🏖️ Walk to the beach, near the Bangsaen roundabout
entries.addr: 22/9 Bang Saen Lang Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi
entries.storyHtml: Bangsaen isn't only the packed main beach — a little further south is Wonnapha Beach with an easier vibe, and right here is where Panitar Haus, a small 54-room hotel, sits on Bang Saen Lang Road, a few steps from the sea. We placed it last in the set because it's a 2-star stay with the lowest starting score in the article (around 7.0 on Trip.com and 3.6/5 on TripAdvisor), but it has a clear strength that genuinely delivers value. The star here is the rooftop infinity pool that looks out over the Wonnapha beach and sea in full, which nearly every review names as the highlight — in the late afternoon guests go up to soak, take photos, and sit watching the sunset over the sea. Some rooms are sea-view rooms with a balcony where you open the curtains to the sea, and importantly prices start at just around ฿1,500/night with breakfast included, which leads many to conclude it's "more view than the price." Reviews also praise the clean rooms, soft, comfortable beds, a hotel that still looks new, friendly staff, and a location within walking distance of the beach, near the Bangsaen roundabout and Burapha University. The honest caveat that has to be stated clearly: this zone has bars and restaurants open late, so many guests hear noise around midnight on weekends, plus the room walls are fairly thin and you can hear the next room, the in-room amenities are minimal to match the price, and "beachfront" means a short road-crossing, not opening the door onto the sand. Best for couples, groups of friends, or small families who want an affordable seaside stay with a great-view rooftop pool to soak in and watch the sunset, accepting the noise and the simplicity of the rooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Go up to the rooftop pool in the late afternoon for the sunset window, the highlight every review mentions · pay extra for a Sea View room with a balcony · if you're sensitive to noise, ask for a high floor away from the bar side and bring earplugs.

The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms; we didn't stay ourselves. The Tide Resort Bangsaen has rebranded as Amari Bangsaen — it's the same place, the same building and pools; when booking, search for "Amari Bangsaen (Formerly The Tide Resort)". Bangsaen has two beach zones: main Bangsaen Beach (lively) and Wonnapha Beach (quieter). On long weekends and weekends Bangsaen gets very crowded, rooms fill fast, and prices rise, so book ahead. Bangsaen has no train line, so having your own car is easiest — about an hour and a half from Bangkok. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers often ask about Bangsaen beachfront stays

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best Bangsaen beachfront stay?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. By score and being a true beachfront resort, The Tide Resort Bangsaen (now Amari Bangsaen) has the highest score in the article at 9.2, you cross the road to the sea, and it has two pools. If you want a sea-view room with a kitchen for a long stay, BBG Seaside has a sea view and kitchen in every room. If you're focused on a sea-view room in the low thousands, Coco Beach Resort. If you like design, Kalm Bangsaen. If you're coming as a family and want a villa, Bangsaen Heritage.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Bangsaen beachfront stays cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿1,300–2,300 per night. On the budget side it's Coasta at ฿1,300 and Coco Beach / Le Casa / Bangsaen Heritage / Panitar Haus starting around ฿1,500. Mid-range is ONPA at ฿1,700 and Kalm at ฿1,800. At the top are BBG at ฿2,000 and The Tide at ฿2,300. All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms; on long weekends and festivals prices move up fast and rooms fill quickly.

faq.q: ❓ Which zone is better in Bangsaen, main Bangsaen Beach or Wonnapha Beach?
faq.a: Main Bangsaen Beach (around the roundabout) is lively, with plenty of restaurants and beachside food, easy to walk down to the sea and head out to eat, good for those who want a lively vibe (The Tide, Coco Beach, Bangsaen Heritage, Kalm, Le Casa). Wonnapha Beach (to the south, near Burapha Univ.) is quieter and more private, good for those who want a calm break (BBG, ONPA, Coasta, Panitar Haus). The two zones are close together, just a few minutes' walk or drive apart.

faq.q: ❓ Are The Tide Resort and Amari Bangsaen the same place?
faq.a: Yes, it's the same place. The resort was formerly called The Tide Resort Bangsaen and has now rebranded as Amari Bangsaen under ONYX Hospitality. The building, pools, and location are the same; when booking on various platforms, search for "Amari Bangsaen (Formerly The Tide Resort Bangsaen)" to avoid confusion. During the transition, some service standards are still adjusting.

faq.q: ❓ Which Bangsaen stay is good for families with kids?
faq.a: The standouts for kids are The Tide Resort and Bangsaen Heritage, which have a pool with a slide and a separate kids' pool. Bangsaen Heritage also has villas to stay in together, some with a private pool, good for big groups. ONPA and Le Casa suit families who want a spacious room with a kitchen to cook in and convenient parking. All of the above have free parking, good for people driving from Bangkok.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a Bangsaen stay?
faq.a: Bangsaen is a beach close to Bangkok that Thai travelers love, so rooms fill fast, especially beachfront stays with limited sea-view rooms (e.g. Coco Beach ~10 rooms, Kalm 21 rooms). On weekends, long weekends, and festivals, book several weeks to a month ahead and arrive early, because the beach road gets congested and parking fills fast. On weekdays, 1–2 weeks is enough. Every platform has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in that kind of rate first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
